Créé en 2014 par Antoine Piombino, Micka: Created in 2014 by Antoine Piombino, Mickael Moretto and Greg Cook, 2 Heures de Perdues ("2 Hours Wasted") — aka 2HDP — ruled French film podcasting for ten years. The concept, inspired by the American "How Did This Get Made?", is simple and irresistible: friends who love films, not academics, draw a film at random from listeners' suggestions and dissect it scene by scene with humour, proudly bad faith and zero filter. Over the seasons, the team grew to include Barbara, Eve, Julie, Sarah, Léa, Jérôme and Olivier, plus regular guests.
En dix saisons et 339 épisodes, l'aventu: Over ten seasons and 339 episodes, this purely amateur adventure grew to fill ever bigger venues — the Bataclan several times, then the Olympia for the final episode, recorded in front of a packed house on Star Wars: Return of the Jedi. The page turned in 2024, but the archive remains intact and as cult as ever.
C'est Lolo qui porte cet épisode avec un: Lolo carries this episode with genuine affection for 2HDP. His analysis pinpoints what made the podcast unique: not the quality of its film criticism — deliberately non-existent — but the listener's feeling of being part of the gang. An evening at a friend's place, proud digressions, inside jokes, cross-references, and well-honed rituals like the Allociné reviews picked apart at the end of each episode.
Le parallèle avec le Floodcast s'impose: The parallel with Floodcast comes naturally: same amateur energy, same tight-knit community, same path to big venues. Lolo has a particular soft spot for seasons 3 and 4, before Mickael Moretto's departure changed the slightly chaotic DNA that gave the early days their charm. A small note of bitterness: the absence of Antoine Piombino — the conductor of the first eight seasons — at the final curtain at the Olympia.
« 2HDP, c'est le podcast zombie par exce: “2HDP is the ultimate zombie podcast — finished, yet still alive, because we keep watching and rewatching the films they reviewed.” — Lolo
